name: Classic Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
instructions: Boil salted water in a large pot. Cook spaghetti until al dente (8-10 min). Reserve 1 cup pasta water.
Thinly slice garlic. In a wide pan, heat olive oil over medium-low heat.
Add garlic and chili flakes. Cook gently 2-3 min until garlic is golden — do NOT burn.
Add drained pasta to the pan with a splash of pasta water. Toss vigorously to emulsify.
Season with salt and pepper. Garnish with fresh parsley and serve immediately.
tips: The pasta water starch is key to creating a creamy sauce — don't skip it.
Low heat for garlic is crucial; burnt garlic makes the dish bitter.
Use the best olive oil you have — it's the star of this dish.

name: Chickpea and Spinach Curry
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter 30 seconds.
Add diced onion and cook 5-6 min until golden. Add minced garlic and grated ginger, cook 1 min.
Add turmeric and garam masala, stir 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in canned tomatoes, crush them, and simmer 5 min.
Add drained chickpeas and coconut milk. Simmer 10 min.
Stir in spinach until wilted (2 min). Season with salt. Serve with rice or naan.
tips: Blooming spices in oil before adding other ingredients unlocks deeper flavor.
Drain and rinse canned chickpeas to reduce sodium.
Leftovers taste even better the next day as flavors meld.

name: Classic Omelette
instructions: Crack eggs into a bowl. Add salt and pepper. Beat with a fork until yolk and white are fully combined.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add butter and let it foam.
Pour in eggs. Let set 10 seconds, then use a spatula to push edges toward center, tilting pan.
When egg is mostly set but still glossy on top (not runny), add cheese if using.
Fold omelette in thirds or roll toward edge of pan. Slide onto plate. Garnish with chives.

cheese: any melting cheese — cheddar, gruyere, mozzarella

tips: Do not over-beat eggs — a few streaks are fine and give better texture.
A hot pan and fast movement are the secrets to a soft, custardy omelette.
Fillings should be pre-cooked; the omelette time is too short to cook raw fillings.

name: Vegetable Fried Rice
instructions: Dice carrot into small cubes. Mince garlic. Slice spring onions, separating white and green parts.
Heat oil in a wok or large pan over high heat. Add garlic and white spring onion parts, stir-fry 30 sec.
Add carrot and peas. Stir-fry 2-3 min.
Push vegetables to one side. Scramble eggs in the empty space until just set.
Add day-old rice, breaking up clumps. Toss everything together on high heat 3-4 min.
Add soy sauce, sesame oil, and salt. Toss again 1 min. Garnish with green spring onion tops.
tips: Day-old cold rice is essential — fresh rice is too moist and makes fried rice gluey.
High heat and a dry wok are the keys to authentic wok hei (smoky flavor).
Add a splash of oyster sauce or fish sauce (if not vegan) for extra depth.

name: Banana Pancakes
instructions: Mash bananas in a bowl until smooth. Beat in eggs until well combined.
Add flour, baking powder, and salt. Mix until just combined — small lumps are fine.
Stir in milk and vanilla extract until batter is smooth.
Heat butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pour 1/4 cup batter per pancake. Cook 2-3 min until bubbles form, then flip and cook 1-2 min.
Serve with honey, maple syrup, or fresh fruit.

eggs: flax egg (1 tbsp ground flax + 3 tbsp water, for vegan)

tips: The riper the banana (spotted/brown), the sweeter and more flavorful the pancakes.
Do not overmix batter — this develops gluten and makes pancakes tough.
For extra fluffy pancakes, let the batter rest 5 min before cooking.

name: Lemon Garlic Roasted Chicken
instructions: Preheat oven to 200C (400F). Pat chicken completely dry with paper towels.
Mix olive oil, juice of 1 lemon, minced garlic, paprika, salt, and pepper into a paste.
Rub paste all over chicken, including under the skin if possible.
Stuff cavity (or surround pieces) with sliced lemon, rosemary, and thyme.
Roast 60-70 min (whole bird) or 35-40 min (pieces) until juices run clear (75C internal temp).
Rest 10 min before carving. Deglaze pan drippings with a splash of water for a quick sauce.
tips: Dry chicken roasts better — moisture prevents crisping of skin.
Room-temperature chicken cooks more evenly than straight from the fridge.
A meat thermometer is the only reliable way to know if chicken is cooked safely.

name: Tomato Basil Soup
instructions: Heat olive oil in a pot over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook 5 min until soft.
Add minced garlic and cook 1 min more.
Add canned tomatoes (crush them with your hands as you add), broth, and sugar.
Simmer 20 min. Remove from heat and add most of the basil.
Blend smooth with an immersion blender or in batches in a blender.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve with remaining basil leaves and a drizzle of olive oil.

sugar: carrot (add while cooking for natural sweetness)

tips: A pinch of sugar balances the acidity of canned tomatoes beautifully.
For a creamy version, stir in 2 tbsp cream or coconut cream before serving.
Pair with crusty bread or a grilled cheese sandwich for a classic combination.

name: Greek Salad
instructions: Chop cucumber into chunky half-moons. Cut tomatoes into wedges. Thinly slice red onion.
Combine cucumber, tomatoes, red onion, and olives in a large bowl.
Drizzle generously with olive oil. Season with salt, pepper, and dried oregano.
Toss gently. Place feta as a large block on top (traditional) or crumble over.
Serve immediately or refrigerate up to 1 hour.
tips: Never dress a Greek salad with lemon juice — authentic Greek salad uses only olive oil.
Pat tomatoes dry for a less watery salad.
The key is chunky cuts — this is not a finely chopped salad.

name: Dal (Red Lentil Soup)
instructions: Rinse lentils until water runs clear. Heat oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add onion and cook 5 min until golden. Add garlic and ginger, cook 1 min.
Add turmeric, cumin, and coriander powder. Stir 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes and cook 3 min. Add rinsed lentils and broth.
Bring to boil, then simmer 15-20 min until lentils are completely soft and creamy.
Stir in lemon juice. Season with salt. Serve garnished with cilantro over rice or with bread.
tips: Red lentils don't need soaking and cook quickly — perfect for weeknights.
For a richer dal, finish with a tarka: fry mustard seeds and curry leaves in ghee, pour over.
Dal thickens as it cools — add water when reheating.

name: Avocado Toast with Poached Egg
instructions: Toast bread until golden and crispy.
Mash avocado with lemon juice, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Bring a pot of water to a gentle simmer. Add white vinegar.
Crack egg into a small cup. Create a gentle whirlpool in the water, then slide egg in.
Poach 3 min for a runny yolk. Remove with a slotted spoon and pat dry.
Spread mashed avocado on toast. Top with poached egg. Sprinkle chili flakes and serve.
tips: Vinegar in poaching water helps the egg white coagulate faster and hold together.
Add a teaspoon of cream cheese under the avocado for extra richness.
Season the avocado well — it needs more salt than you think.

name: Beef Stir-Fry with Vegetables
instructions: Slice beef thinly against the grain. Marinate with 1 tbsp soy sauce and cornstarch for 10 min.
Cut broccoli into florets. Slice bell pepper into strips. Mince garlic and ginger.
Mix remaining soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sesame oil into a sauce bowl.
Heat wok over highest flame until smoking. Add 2 tbsp oil. Sear beef 2-3 min, do not stir too soon. Remove.
Add remaining oil. Stir-fry garlic and ginger 30 sec. Add broccoli and pepper, stir-fry 3-4 min.
Return beef to wok. Pour sauce over. Toss 1-2 min until everything is coated. Serve over rice.

oyster sauce: soy sauce with a pinch of sugar

tips: Slicing meat against the grain shortens muscle fibers, making it tenderer.
Cornstarch in the marinade creates a velvety coating on the meat (velveting technique).
Work fast — stir-fry is a high-heat, quick technique. Have everything prepped before you start.

name: Simple French Toast
instructions: Whisk eggs, milk, vanilla, cinnamon, sugar, and salt together in a shallow bowl.
Heat butter in a pan over medium heat until foaming.
Dip each bread slice in egg mixture, letting it soak 10-15 seconds per side.
Cook each slice 2-3 min per side until golden brown.
Serve immediately with maple syrup, powdered sugar, or fresh berries.
tips: Thick, slightly stale bread absorbs the custard best without falling apart.
Let slices soak longer (30 sec each side) for a custardy interior.
A little orange zest in the custard adds a wonderful brightness.
